To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IFN-γ, a cytokine that is well known for its anti-fibrotical and anti-angiogenetic effect, inhibits CTGF expression and proliferation in human LEC, and that this inhibitory effect is enhanced when IFN-γ is co-applied with TNF-α.
CTGF is down-regulated by IFN-ɣ in LEC via a Jak-Stat signaling and that an additive effect of TNF-α and IFN-γ can be found on the down-regulation of CTGF and LEC proliferation.
IFN-γ inhibits CTGF expression in a Jak/STAT-dependent manner in human LEC, and that IFN- γ and TNF- α act synergistically on inhibition of CTG F expression and cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CTGF and IFN-γ as well as TNF-α in LEC.
the role of IFNs in lung diseases, and in particular with the influence of IFNs on the expression of CTGF, a profibrotic and angiogenetic factor, in lung endothelial and epithelial cells.
the role of IFNs and TNF- α in LEC and their effect on CTGF expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IFN-γ has an inhibitory effect on CTGF expression, which might be beneficial in the context of airway remodeling.
the Th1 cytokine IFN-γ has an anti-fibrotically effect in LEC by down-regulating CTGF expression.
IFN-γ has anti-remodeling and anti-proliferation effects in LEC, which are at least partly mediated by down-regulation of CTGF expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFN-γ is an inhibitor of CTGF expression in lung endothelial cell and this inhibitory effect could be enhanced by TNF-α.
the Th1 response is not only anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrogenic, but it also has an anti-angiogenetic effect in LEC.
IFN-γ is an important anti-inflammatory cytokine in asthma, but its effect is not restricted to the inflammatory cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFN-γ is a strong inhibitor of the profibrotic and angiogenic growth factor CTGF in human lung endothelial cells, and that the inhibitory effects of IFN- γ and TNF- α on CTGF expression are additive.
IFN-γ is a negative regulator of CTGF in human endothelial cells.
CTGF is a negative regulator of LEC proliferation.
